name: Microcline Green
lede: Microcline Green is a very pale green named for microcline, a feldspar mineral whose green variety is better known by its own name, amazonite.

sections.title: A feldspar's pale green
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 color book places this value on plate XIX, hue 39′, tone f, and the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 files it as block 148, very pale green, a block so crowded it also covers names such as Cabbage, Ice Tint and Water Green [1]. Maerz and Paul date a related entry to 1912 as well [1]. Microcline is a common rock-forming feldspar; its green form, colored by trace lead, is better known by its own gem name, amazonite, though this particular library name is undocumented beyond the 1912 citation [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[dull-opaline-green]], [[pale-nile-blue]] and [[lichen-green]], at 3.6, 3.8 and 4.3 ΔE [1]. Compare [[sage|Sage]], [[mint-turquoise|Mint Turquoise]] and [[jade|Jade]], other pale or mineral-named greens [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a color within six units of this one in only 23, about 0.1 percent, as photographed [2]. It covers over half the canvas in Michele Marieschi's 1740 view of Santa Maria della Salute and in Canaletto's 1748 Warwick Castle, both pale Venetian or English skies [2]. It is 15 times more common in Impressionist paintings than in the archive overall, a small but notable lift [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and the match is not a mineral or pigment test [2].
